support. 11. Follow up and learn.

**Lead Generation — leads may come from:** marketing; website or marketplace; field
prospecting; retailer/distributor research; institutional lists; referrals; trade/community
networks; events; customer expansion; creator or campaign response. A list is not a pipeline.
Every lead requires source, relevance, owner, status, and next action.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Qualification
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Qualification area | Consumer/B2B interpretation |
|---|---|
| Need | Is there a real problem or use case? |
| Fit | Does the Muv product/channel suit it? |
| Authority | Who decides or influences? |
| Scale | What realistic requirement exists? |
| Timing | When and why now? |
| Economics | Can the transaction work for both sides? |
| Operations | Can Muv supply, support, and collect? |
| Risk | Credit, return, reputation, compliance, or conflict |

Qualification protects both customer and Muv from forced fit.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Customer Understanding & Sales Conversation
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
identify the buyer and user;
understand current solution; identify decision criteria; understand objections and risk; know
required documentation; know order, delivery, and service needs; identify stakeholders.

**Sales Conversation — a useful conversation:** 1. establishes context; 2. asks and listens; 3.
confirms the problem; 4. explains relevant value; 5. supports the claim; 6. checks
understanding; 7. clarifies commercial conditions; 8. agrees the next step.

> **Sales Rule** — Never promise a product result, delivery, territory, margin, credit, return,
> or support condition that has not been authorised.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Demonstration
Objection Handling
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Listen → Clarify → Classify → Answer with
truth → Confirm → Record → Improve.

| Objection | Appropriate response |
|---|---|
| Value/price | Explain verified value, usage, economics, and alternatives |
| Product performance | Use approved evidence and demonstration |
| Trust | Provide company, product, quality, review, or support information |
| Availability | Give accurate supply status |
| Margin/terms | Use authorised commercial architecture |
| Risk | Clarify trial, service, return, or contract terms where approved |
| Not now | Record timing and next trigger; do not pressure |

An objection that repeats across customers is commercial intelligence.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Follow-Up System & Conversion Discipline
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
send requested information; confirm trial
or sample; answer an open question; review proposal; check supply or decision timing; support
onboarding; review first order/use. Record next action, owner, date, and customer preference.
Persistence without relevance becomes pressure.

**Conversion Discipline requires:** clear product/SKU; quantity; approved price and scheme;
payment/credit condition; delivery; documentation; contact; return/claim understanding; order
confirmation; system entry.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Sales Documentation
Distribution Architecture
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Route | Role |
|---|---|
| D2C | Direct owned customer transaction and data relationship |
| Marketplace | Platform-led discovery, transaction, fulfilment, and reputation |
| Retail | Physical availability and assisted/local purchase |
| Distributor | Territory stock and retailer/institution reach |
| Institutional/B2B | Direct supply to defined organisational use cases |
| Quick commerce | Fast local availability through platform infrastructure |
| Franchise/partner | Governed partner model with defined roles and supply |

Channel selection should follow customer, product, economics, operational capability, and
strategic fit.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Supply Alignment & Partner Selection
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
approved products and packs
available; demand assumptions shared with production; inventory ownership clear; service level
defined; reorder and lead time understood; storage and transport suitable; returns and damaged
goods controlled; data and reconciliation ready.

**Partner Selection — assess:** market and customer access; reputation; infrastructure;
category capability; financial and credit strength; operating discipline; data and
communication capability; conflict risk; willingness to follow Muv standards; long-term fit.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Partner Onboarding
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Qualification → Due diligence →
Commercial approval → Agreement → Product/brand training → Systems and territory setup →
Opening stock → Activation → Review.

**Provide:** company and product understanding; approved price and scheme; territory/channel
scope; ordering and payment; inventory and storage; claims and communication;
returns/complaints; reporting; escalation; review cadence.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Distributor & Retailer Relationships & Institutional Partnerships
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
reliable
supply; clear commercial rules; honest communication; sell-through support; stock visibility;
fair issue resolution; no hidden channel conflict; regular review. Do not load inventory into a
channel without a realistic sell-through and service plan.

**Institutional Partnerships — institutional sales may require:** use-case diagnosis; approved
samples or trials; product and quality documentation; usage and dosage; supply schedule;
training; site or account support; commercial proposal; contract and service responsibilities.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Conflict Management
Geographic Expansion & Pilot Markets
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Market hypothesis → Readiness assessment
→ Pilot territory → Local learning → Controlled channel scale → Regional repeatability →
National expansion.

**Expansion decisions should consider:** customer demand; product relevance; competition and
price; supply and service; local partners; marketing support; unit economics; compliance;
learning capacity.

**Pilot Markets — a pilot should define:** geography; customer and channel; product range;
partner and supply plan; price; marketing; service; metrics; duration; scale/stop conditions.
Local learning must be recorded before broader expansion.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Sales Training
Chapter Governance Summary
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
**Common Mistakes:** Treating all leads as equal. Presenting before understanding. Pressuring
customers who lack fit. Leaving commercial promises outside the CRM. Appointing partners only
for reach. Shipping opening stock without sell-through support. Expanding before supply and
service readiness.

**Best Practices:** Qualify early and respectfully. Make next steps explicit. Record repeated
objections. Align sales commitments with inventory and manufacturing. Train partners before
activation. Pilot territories with scale and stop criteria. Review partner sell-through, not
only sell-in.

**Action Checklist:**
- [ ] Lead source, fit, owner, and stage recorded.
- [ ] Customer/partner need and authority understood.
- [ ] Product value and demonstration approved.
- [ ] Objections and open questions documented.
- [ ] Price, terms, supply, and service authorised.
- [ ] Order and follow-up controlled.
- [ ] Channel selection supported by economics and capability.
- [ ] Partner due diligence and onboarding complete.
- [ ] Territory and conflict rules clear.
- [ ] Pilot market has metrics and decision conditions.
- [ ] Sales and partner training verified.

**Key Takeaways:** Sales helps relevant buyers decide; it does not force fit. Distribution is a
designed route-to-market system. Partner reach matters only when economics, operations, trust,
and sell-through align. Expansion should move through controlled local learning.

**Chapter Summary:** *"Sales & Distribution converts market interest into qualified
conversations, authorised transactions, reliable channel execution, and disciplined
expansion."* Source's own transition line: *"Next: Marketplace Operations governs platform
setup, listings, inventory, orders, service, settlements, and operational reliability"* — the
sourced justification for Chapter 3 following next.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Marketplace Philosophy & Channel Selection
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
A marketplace is a commercial operating system, not merely another webpage. It
combines: platform rules; catalogue and content; inventory; price; fulfilment; advertising;
customer questions and reviews; returns and claims; settlements; account health.

**Figure 3.1 — Marketplace Operating System:** Approved SKU → Catalogue/listing → Inventory →
Discovery → Conversion → Order → Fulfilment → Delivery → Review/return → Settlement →
Learning. Failure in one component can damage the complete channel.

**Channel Selection — before joining or expanding on a platform, assess:** target customer
presence; category fit; fee and fulfilment structure; pricing and promotion; service-level
requirements; return risk; content capability; advertising need; inventory placement; data
access; account-governance capacity. Presence is not automatically profitable distribution.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Account Governance
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
legal and business identity; authorised users and roles; security and
recovery; bank/tax/commercial records; brand or catalogue permissions; notification ownership;
policy and account-health monitoring; access review; escalation. Never allow critical platform
ownership to remain with one ungoverned personal account.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Catalogue & SKU Setup & Listing Version Control
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
match canonical product/SKU; use
correct category; verify brand and name; verify size, variant, and pack count; use approved
identifier/barcode where applicable; align MRP and selling-price control; link current product
information and assets; record listing ID and relationship to variants.

**Listing Version Control — maintain:**

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Platform/listing ID | Unique channel identity |
| Canonical SKU | Link to Muv product master |
| Content version | Identify current title, bullets, description, and images |
| Price version | Align commercial state |
| Inventory model | Seller/fulfilment ownership |
| Status | Draft, active, suppressed, blocked, retired |
| Owner | Accountability |
| Last review | Recency |

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Inventory Architecture & Demand & Replenishment
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
available;
reserved; in transit; platform fulfilment stock; damaged; returned; unsellable; under
investigation; ageing. Reconcile Muv records with platform records. Platform availability
without physical or ownership clarity creates overselling, cost, and customer harm.

**Demand & Replenishment — plan from:** historic sales with context; active campaign and
promotion; seasonality; lead time; platform replenishment time; safety stock logic;
expiry/shelf considerations where relevant; return and damage; cash and storage constraints.
Avoid both stock-out and uncontrolled stock loading.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Order & Fulfilment & Fulfilment Model
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Order received → Payment/status verified →
Inventory allocated → Pick → Product/SKU check → Pack → Label/document → Handover → Tracking →
Delivery → Closure.

**Control:** correct item and quantity; product and pack condition; current channel packaging
requirements; shipping label; dispatch SLA; scan and handover; tracking exception; failed
delivery; return.

**Fulfilment Model — compare:**

| Seller fulfilment | Platform fulfilment |
|---|---|
| More direct operational control | Platform storage/dispatch structure |
| Requires Muv pick-pack and SLA capability | Requires inbound and platform inventory governance |
| Different cost and service risks | Different fees, ageing, return, and reconciliation risks |

Select according to customer service, economics, control, capacity, and product needs.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Marketplace Pricing & Promotions
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
platform
fees; fulfilment/shipping; storage; ads; returns and claims; discounts/coupons; tax;
settlements; channel conflict; realised contribution. Do not judge profitability from the
displayed selling price.

**Promotions — before a marketplace deal:** define objective; confirm inventory; calculate
complete economics; align price and channel policy; prepare listing and advertising; define
period; monitor service and account risk; record result.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Reviews, Questions & Reputation
Returns & Claims
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
wrong item; damage/leakage; delivery failure; listing mismatch;
product complaint; misuse or expectation mismatch; fraud/abuse; platform handling issue. Link
returns to exact SKU, batch when available, order, listing, fulfilment, and customer evidence.
Update sellable status correctly.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Settlement & Reconciliation & Account Health
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Orders → Cancellations →
Returns/refunds → Platform fees → Ads/promotions → Claims/reimbursements → Taxes → Net
settlement → Ledger/reconciliation. Commercial teams must understand why net settlement
differs from gross order value.

**Account Health — monitor:** listing compliance/suppression; cancellation; late dispatch;
tracking; order defects; customer claims; returns; inventory; policy notifications; rights or
catalogue issues. Correct root causes, not only the visible score.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Quick-Commerce Readiness
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
city-level inventory; high availability expectation;
compressed product content; rapid replenishment; platform/warehouse coordination; local demand
and promotion; tight reconciliation. Launch only when the SKU, supply, economics, and local
operating owner are ready.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Chapter Governance Summary
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
**Common Mistakes:** Creating duplicate listings for the same SKU. Treating platform inventory
as fully reconciled. Running deals without complete contribution analysis. Advertising an
out-of-stock or weak listing. Ignoring suppressed listings and policy notifications. Returning
questionable stock to sellable inventory without control. Reporting gross sales as net channel
performance.

**Best Practices:** Maintain one canonical listing register. Audit product, content, price, and
inventory together. Forecast campaigns with operations. Reconcile orders, inventory, returns,
fees, and settlements. Link review and return patterns to product and service owners. Assign
account-health ownership.

**Action Checklist:**
- [ ] Platform fit and economics assessed.
- [ ] Account ownership, access, and security controlled.
- [ ] Canonical SKU and listing identity aligned.
- [ ] Product, price, images, and content current.
- [ ] Inventory states reconciled.
- [ ] Replenishment plan approved.
- [ ] Order and fulfilment controls operating.
- [ ] Promotions use complete economics.
- [ ] Reviews, questions, returns, and claims routed.
- [ ] Settlements reconciled.
- [ ] Account health monitored.
- [ ] Quick-commerce expansion is locally ready.

**Key Takeaways:** Marketplace selling combines catalogue, inventory, fulfilment, pricing,
reputation, and finance. The listing, SKU, stock, order, return, and settlement must remain
connected. Displayed revenue is not realised contribution. Quick commerce requires local
operational readiness, not only listing access.

**Chapter Summary:** *"Marketplace Operations establishes the commercial and operational
controls needed to sell reliably through Amazon, Flipkart, quick commerce, and related
platforms."* Source's own transition line: *"Next: Marketplace Content & Conversion governs how
accurate commercial information becomes confident customer action"* — the sourced
justification for Chapter 4 following next.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Conversion Philosophy & Listing Information Architecture
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Conversion should be the result of informed confidence, not missing information or
pressure.

**Figure 4.1 — Marketplace Conversion Path:** Relevant discovery → Accurate recognition →
Clear value → Credible proof → Suitable price/availability → Low-friction choice → Reliable
fulfilment. Content cannot compensate permanently for poor product, price, stock, delivery, or
reviews.

**Listing Information Architecture:**

| Listing element | Customer job |
|---|---|
| Title | Identify exact product, type, variant, size, and relevant approved descriptor |
| Hero image | Confirm exact product and pack |
| Supporting images | Explain benefits, use, details, context, and trust |
| Bullets/key features | Enable rapid evaluation |
| Description/A+ | Provide deeper product and brand understanding |
| Variant relationship | Help customers select correctly |
| Price/offer | Clarify current commercial choice |
| Reviews/questions | Provide social proof and uncertainty reduction |
| Delivery/availability | Set transaction expectation |

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Product Listing Philosophy & Title Discipline
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
What exactly is this? Is it relevant to my problem or
use? What approved value does it provide? How do I use it? Which size or variant should I
choose? Why should I trust Muv and this product? What will I pay and receive?

**Title Discipline — titles should be:** accurate; channel-compliant; customer-readable;
consistent with label and product master; differentiated by relevant attributes; free from
unsupported keyword stuffing and claims.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Image Communication & Content & Claim Control
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
1. Exact product hero. 2. Primary
approved value. 3. Key benefits. 4. Product/use context. 5. How to use. 6. Relevant detail or
ingredient information. 7. Trust, variant, size, or comparison information. Image roles may
change by product and platform. Product truth from Volume IV remains protected.

**Content & Claim Control — every product fact should have an owning source:** Volume V for
product and claims; Volume IV for pack and image truth; Chapter 1 for price; Chapter 3 for
availability and fulfilment; Volume III for identity and voice.

> **Distribution Rule** — A platform text field does not authorise a new product claim.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Search Discoverability & Mobile-First Evaluation
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
real customer language; exact
product/category terms; variant and size; approved use or benefit terms; attributes that
support correct selection. Do not use unrelated brand names, false comparisons, or unsupported
benefits to gain discovery.

**Mobile-First Evaluation — prioritise:** immediate product recognition; readable image text;
one message per image; concise bullets; clear variant/size; visible rating/review context;
accurate delivery and offer.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Product Detail Page Quality Gate
Reviews & Reputation & Questions & Answers
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
understand recurring strengths; identify
unanswered questions; detect listing mismatch; identify delivery/packaging issues; route
product concerns; improve instructions and content. Never fabricate, purchase, coerce, or
selectively misrepresent reviews.

**Questions & Answers — create a controlled answer library for recurring questions, but
check:** exact product; current formula/pack; approved claim; use; channel rules; date. When
uncertain, escalate rather than improvise publicly.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Offer Communication
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
eligible product/variant; price or benefit; quantity
or threshold; dates; channel; conditions; stock limitations where appropriate. Avoid fake
urgency or permanently recurring "limited" claims.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Conversion Diagnostics
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Signal | Possible investigation |
|---|---|
| Impressions low | Discovery, category, availability, ranking, advertising |
| Click-through low | Hero, title, relevance, price, rating |
| Detail views but conversion low | Value, proof, price, delivery, reviews, variants, trust |
| Add-to-cart but order low | Price change, delivery, payment, competition, stock |
| Orders but high returns | Listing mismatch, product, pack, delivery, expectation |
| Sales but low repeat | Product/customer fit, experience, use, value |

These are diagnostic directions, not automatic causes.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Listing Experiments
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
hero framing; approved benefit
hierarchy; image order; title clarity; bullet sequence; offer; advertising placement.
**Protect:** product truth; identity; claim compliance; customer quality; returns; channel
economics.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Chapter Governance Summary
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
**Common Mistakes:** Using the wrong bottle or label in the hero image. Hiding important
product differences. Writing for the algorithm rather than the customer. Overloading image
text. Leaving price or pack information inconsistent. Treating conversion increase as success
despite rising returns. Testing multiple elements without a hypothesis.

**Best Practices:** Build listings from canonical product sources. Review the full mobile
journey. Give each image one job. Use review questions to improve education. Diagnose
conversion by stage. Evaluate experiments with return and customer-quality guardrails.

**Action Checklist:**
- [ ] Exact SKU, product, variant, size, and pack verified.
- [ ] Title and category accurate.
- [ ] Hero and supporting images preserve product truth.
- [ ] Claims link to approved evidence.
- [ ] Search terms are relevant and honest.
- [ ] Bullets and description answer customer questions.
- [ ] Price, offer, stock, and delivery current.
- [ ] Reviews and Q&A monitored.
- [ ] Mobile presentation checked.
- [ ] Conversion diagnostics include returns and repeat.
- [ ] Experiments are controlled.
- [ ] Other channels remain consistent.

**Key Takeaways:** Conversion should express informed confidence. Marketplace content must
connect product, price, stock, proof, reviews, and fulfilment. Search optimisation cannot
weaken customer truth. Conversion quality includes returns, repeat, and long-term trust.

**Chapter Summary:** *"Marketplace Content & Conversion gives customers the information needed
to identify, evaluate, and purchase the correct Muv product while keeping channel performance
anchored to truth."* Source's own transition line: *"Next: Commercial Decisions & Channel
Evolution governs revenue intelligence, forecasting, targets, incentives, CRM, expansion, and
future leadership"* — the sourced justification for Chapter 5 following next, and independent
confirmation that Chapter 5 will need to handle the CRM content already excerpted in Domain 3.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Decision Integrity
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
The canonical Volume VIII evidence contains pricing, sales, distribution,
Amazon/Flipkart, online-selling, and channel discussions with multiple Decision Records.
Authority remains attached to exact evidence and version.

Sales targets, marketing budgets, marketplace suggestions, institutional pitches, price ideas,
partner economics, and expansion concepts must not be converted into permanent approved
commercial rules merely because they appear specific.

> **Sales Rule** — Specific numbers are not automatically approved numbers. Every price,
> target, margin, fee, forecast, and incentive must retain source, date, assumptions, scope,
> and authority.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Revenue Intelligence System & Revenue Planning
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Market potential → Pipeline → Forecast
→ Supply plan → Orders → Fulfilment → Collection/settlement → Returns/claims → Contribution →
Repeat → Decision. Revenue intelligence connects demand with operational and economic reality.

**Revenue Planning — plan revenue by:** product/SKU; channel; customer/account type;
territory; time; quantity; price; promotion; return/cancellation; fulfilment; collection;
contribution. Distinguish aspiration, target, forecast, order, shipment, delivery, invoice,
collection, and realised net revenue.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Sales Forecasting
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Forecast input | Control |
|---|---|
| Historical sales | Adjust for stock-outs, promotions, launches, and anomalies |
| Pipeline | Weight by defined stage and evidence |
| Customer commitment | Separate conversation, intent, PO, and paid order |
| Marketing | Include campaign timing and uncertainty |
| Seasonality | Use supported patterns |
| Channel inventory | Include sell-in, sell-through, and stock ageing |
| Supply | Include capacity, material, lead time, and release |
| Price/promotion | Reflect approved changes |

Forecasts should be reviewed against actual outcomes to improve calibration.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Targets & Incentives
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
connected to market and capacity; broken into controllable
units; clear by role and period; economically responsible; balanced with customer and quality
outcomes; reviewed without encouraging manipulation. **A target should not reward:**
uncollectable billing; channel stuffing; unauthorised discounts; weak-fit customers; hidden
returns; false claims.

**Incentives should align:** revenue quality; contribution; collection; sell-through;
retention; customer experience; documentation; ethical conduct.

> **WARNING** — An incentive can become a hidden operating policy. Review what behaviour it
> actually produces.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Sales Metrics
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Area | Metrics |
|---|---|
| Activity | Relevant calls, meetings, demonstrations, follow-ups |
| Pipeline | Qualified value, stage, ageing, conversion |
| Revenue | Orders, delivered sales, net realised revenue |
| Economics | Gross contribution, channel cost, discount, return, credit |
| Distribution | Active partners/outlets, availability, stock, sell-through |
| Customer | Repeat, complaint, retention, account health |
| Execution | Fill rate, on-time delivery, collection, forecast accuracy |

Metrics must have definitions and owners.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Customer Acquisition Economics
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
marketing acquisition cost; sales
effort; samples/demonstrations; onboarding; discounts; credit; fulfilment; returns; support;
retention and contribution. For B2B or institutional relationships, account-acquisition cost
and time-to-value may be more useful than a consumer CAC alone.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Territory Planning

knowledgeItemProjections.title: CRM System (Citation Only — Content Held by Domain 3)
Sales Documentation
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
sales process and stage definitions; price list
and scheme; product and pitch assets; quotation/proposal templates; partner assessment;
onboarding and agreement records; territory plan; forecast; target/incentive plan; account
review; channel decision; commercial exception and approval; training.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Commercial Decision Record
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Decision ID | Stable identifier |
| Subject | Price, customer, channel, territory, partner, target, exception, or expansion |
| Authority/date | Who decided and when |
| Question | Exact commercial issue |
| Evidence | Customer, product, economics, supply, risk, and history |
| Alternatives | Options considered |
| Status | Approved, partially approved, rejected, deferred, research required, open, or superseded |
| Rationale | Evidence-supported reason |
| Conditions | Time, territory, volume, credit, review, or dependency |
| Effect | Systems, price lists, agreements, listings, forecasts, and teams affected |

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Channel Evolution
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Channels evolve when customer, product, economics, capability, or strategy
changes. **A channel may:** begin as a pilot; expand by geography or portfolio; change
fulfilment model; require new partner roles; become less viable; create conflict; be paused or
exited. Preserve earlier architecture and the reason for change.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Expansion & Market Development
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
National expansion should not be a single leap.

**Figure 5.5 — Commercial Expansion Path:** Local proof → Repeatable territory model →
Regional system → Multi-region governance → National network.

**Before each stage:** product demand and repeat supported; supply and quality reliable;
channel economics proven; partner model repeatable; customer service scalable; inventory and
cash implications understood; documentation and training transferable.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Franchise & Partnership Support
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
opportunity explanation; approved
investment/economic information; product and supply model; role and responsibility; territory;
brand and marketing assets; training; operating handoffs; reporting; performance review.
Franchise/legal and capital architecture belong to their owning volumes. Never market a
projection or ROI as guaranteed.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Partner Performance Review
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Area | Question |
|---|---|
| Sales | Is sell-through healthy and appropriately distributed? |
| Inventory | Is stock sufficient, ageing, damaged, or overloaded? |
| Economics | Are agreed terms producing sustainable results? |
| Coverage | Is the intended market actually served? |
| Execution | Are ordering, payment, storage, claims, and reporting disciplined? |
| Brand/product | Are approved identity and claims protected? |
| Customer | What feedback and complaints exist? |
| Relationship | Are communication and conflict handled well? |

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Knowledge Transfer
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
account and
relationship history; current opportunities; commitments and exceptions; prices and terms;
open issues; inventory and collection; next actions; risks; decision rationale. No commercial
relationship should exist only in one person's phone or memory.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Sales Team Development
Future Commercial Leadership & Sustainable Revenue Culture
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
Revenue +
Contribution + Collection + Availability + Customer trust + Partner health + Long-term
capability. **They should ask:** Is revenue real, collectible, and economically useful? Are we
helping the right customer? Are partners selling through or only buying in? Are discounts
solving a strategic problem or hiding weak value? Can manufacturing and service support the
plan? What should we stop, pilot, or scale?

**Sustainable Revenue Culture — a sustainable culture:** tells the truth; records commitments;
respects authority; learns from lost sales; avoids blame-driven forecasting; rewards customer
and partner quality; refuses channel stuffing; protects cross-functional trust; compounds
reliable relationships.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Chapter Governance Summary
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
**Common Mistakes:** Treating aspiration as forecast. Counting orders before fulfilment or
collection. Designing incentives around gross billing alone. Leaving exception pricing
undocumented. Using CRM as surveillance instead of commercial memory. Scaling a channel before
unit economics and service are proven. Allowing one salesperson to own all relationship
knowledge.

**Best Practices:** Use common commercial definitions. Forecast by evidence and stage. Balance
targets with quality and collection. Review realised contribution by channel. Keep price and
exception approvals traceable. Pilot before national expansion. Make commercial handovers
routine.

**Action Checklist:**
- [ ] Revenue plan distinguishes target, forecast, order, delivery, collection, and net realisation.
- [ ] Forecast assumptions and stage definitions documented.
- [ ] Targets protect quality, contribution, and customer trust.
- [ ] Incentives tested for unintended behaviour.
- [ ] Metrics have definitions and owners.
- [ ] Acquisition economics include sales and service cost.
- [ ] Territory plans align with supply and partner capability.
- [ ] CRM preserves relationship and commitment history.
- [ ] Commercial decisions and exceptions recorded.
- [ ] Channel evolution links old and new states.
- [ ] Expansion stages have proof and stop conditions.
- [ ] Team knowledge transfers without dependence on one person.

**Key Takeaways:** Revenue intelligence follows value from pipeline through collection and
repeat. Targets and incentives must produce healthy behaviour. CRM preserves commercial memory
and accountability. Expansion becomes sustainable when local proof becomes a repeatable
operating model.

**Chapter Summary:** *"Commercial Decisions & Channel Evolution turns sales activity into
governed revenue intelligence. It gives Muv the forecasting, metrics, CRM, leadership, and
learning systems required to scale reach without weakening economics or trust."* Source's own
transition line: *"Next: Volume IX continues the Knowledge Library with MUV Customer
Experience™—the operating system for customer interaction, service, support, recovery, and
long-term relationship quality"* — Part IX is fully covered by Domain 3 (frozen); cited here for
completeness, never re-transcribed.

knowledgeItemProjections.title: Part VIII Summary: MUV Sales & Distribution System in One View
knowledgeItemProjections.content:
| Commercial area | Permanent standard |
|---|---|
| Philosophy | Help relevant buyers make confident, value-based decisions |
| Pricing | Align product cost, customer value, channel economics, and governance |
| Sales | Qualify, understand, demonstrate, clarify, follow up, and fulfil |
| Distribution | Place the right product through a viable and reliable route |
| Partners | Select, onboard, train, support, and review with clear boundaries |
| Marketplaces | Connect catalogue, stock, orders, fulfilment, returns, settlements, and health |
| Conversion | Create informed confidence through accurate content and commercial readiness |
| Revenue | Distinguish aspiration, forecast, order, delivery, collection, and contribution |
| Territory | Expand through controlled local learning |
| CRM | Preserve relationship, commitment, opportunity, and decision history |
| Governance | Keep prices, terms, exceptions, channels, and authority traceable |
| Leadership | Balance revenue with customer, partner, supply, and long-term capability |

**Master Commercial Principles:** 1. Value before pressure. 2. Qualification before
presentation. 3. Authorised promise before commitment. 4. Complete economics before price or
promotion. 5. Sell-through before channel loading. 6. Availability and fulfilment before
expansion. 7. Accurate listing before advertising. 8. Collection and contribution before
revenue celebration. 9. Document every important commercial exception. 10. Scale only what can
remain reliable.

**Master Commercial Checklist:**
- [ ] Product, price, and channel versions aligned.
- [ ] Complete cost and contribution basis verified.
- [ ] Customer/partner qualified.
- [ ] Sales conversation and demonstration use approved value.
- [ ] Terms, credit, supply, returns, and support authorised.
- [ ] Order, fulfilment, collection, and feedback connected.
- [ ] Partner selection and onboarding complete.
- [ ] Territory/channel conflicts controlled.
- [ ] Marketplace listing, inventory, orders, returns, and settlements reconciled.
- [ ] Content and claims accurate.
- [ ] Forecast, target, and metric definitions current.
- [ ] Incentives support healthy behaviour.
- [ ] CRM and decision records complete.
- [ ] Expansion pilot evidence reviewed.
- [ ] Commercial knowledge transferable.

**Part End Note (verbatim):** *"Volume VIII establishes MUV Sales & Distribution System™ as the
official commercial operating system for pricing, sales execution, distribution, marketplaces,
partnerships, revenue intelligence, expansion, and commercial governance. Muv commercial growth
must remain rooted in real product value, confident customer decisions, reliable fulfilment,
sustainable economics, and relationships that strengthen over time. Volume IX continues the MUV
Knowledge Library™ with MUV Customer Experience™."* Part IX is fully covered by Domain 3
(frozen) and is cited here only for completeness, not transcribed.

sections.purpose:
MUV Liquid Detergent™ is formulated as a liquid laundry cleaning product intended to remove
soil, stains, and odour from fabric during washing. The formulation is a surfactant-based liquid
system (see `03_Manufacturing.md` for the full raw-material list) combined with a fragrance and
colour identity unique to each of the three variants.

**Not yet available (REQUIRES FOUNDER INPUT):**
- Any specific performance claim (e.g. "removes 99% of stains," "works in cold water," "safe for
  all fabric types") — none of these appear in any source document found, and none may be
  asserted without Founder-approved, evidence-backed language
- Intended machine type (top-load / front-load / hand-wash) — not stated in the SOP
- Water hardness or dosage-per-load guidance beyond what may exist on retail packaging (not
  found in the repo)
benefits: Helps remove everyday dirt and common stains
Leaves clothes with a fresh Cool Water fragrance
Suitable for machine wash and bucket wash
Liquid formulation mixes conveniently in water
Suitable for regular fabric care
Can support careful stain pre-treatment
Available in 1 L and 5 L packs
sections.usageInstructions:
For machine wash, add approximately 30 ml of Muv Liquid Detergent for a regular load. Adjust the quantity according to load size, fabric condition and level of soiling.

For bucket wash, add a suitable quantity to water, mix well, soak the garments if required, wash gently and rinse thoroughly with clean water.

For difficult stains, apply a small quantity directly to the affected area, gently rub or allow it to remain briefly, and then wash normally.

Always check garment care instructions before washing.
sections.safetyInformation:
Keep out of reach of children.

Avoid contact with eyes. In case of eye contact, rinse thoroughly with clean water.

Do not swallow.

Wash hands after prolonged direct contact.

Test on a small hidden area before using on delicate or colour-sensitive fabrics.

Seek medical advice in case of accidental ingestion or persistent irritation.
sections.storageInstructions:
Store in a cool and dry place away from direct sunlight and excessive heat.

Keep the container tightly closed and upright when not in use.

Do not transfer the product into food or beverage containers.

Protect from contamination and moisture.

intended for toilet bowl cleaning — removing limescale, stains, and soil from ceramic/porcelain

sections.usageInstructions:
Open the cap carefully.

Apply Muv Floral Toilet Cleaner directly inside the toilet bowl, including under the rim and over visibly stained areas.

Allow the cleaner to remain on the surface for approximately 10 minutes.

Scrub thoroughly with a toilet brush.

Flush with clean water.

For difficult deposits, repeat the process if required.
sections.safetyInformation:

Use only for toilet-bowl cleaning.

Avoid contact with skin, eyes and clothing.

Wear suitable protective gloves during prolonged use.

Do not swallow.

Never mix with bleach, acids, ammonia or any other cleaning chemical.

Use in a ventilated area.

In case of eye or skin contact, rinse immediately with plenty of clean water.

Seek medical advice in case of accidental ingestion or significant exposure.

sections.purpose:
MUV Dishwash Gel™ is formulated as a surfactant-based liquid gel intended for hand dishwashing —
removing grease and food soil from dishes/utensils. Unlike the other two product families
audited so far, this product's own QC section directly states a functional pass criterion
("Good foam and grease cleaning"), giving this purpose statement a firmer evidentiary basis than
was possible for Liquid Detergent or Toilet Cleaner.

- Any comparative or superlative performance claim ("cuts grease faster," "gentle on hands," "1
  drop does more") — none appear in any source document
- Water hardness or dilution guidance for actual dishwashing use
- Suitability for dishwashing machines vs. hand-wash only (nothing in the source suggests
  machine use; this is a hand-dishwash-gel formulation by all indications, but this inference is
  not explicitly stated either)
